reviews.text: Routinely deletes all my saved sessions. Drives me nuts.
reviews.dev_reply:
Thanks for the feedback. I understand how frustrating this can be.

Session Buddy stores your data locally in Chrome, which is a deliberate design choice to keep things private and under your control. However, this also means it relies on Chrome’s IndexedDB storage mechanism, which has been known to occasionally lose or corrupt extension data due to browser-level bugs. This isn’t specific to Session Buddy. It's a broader platform issue that Google is actively working to address (you can track progress here: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40253999).

To compensate for this risk and keep your data safe, Session Buddy includes an automatic backup feature. In cases where Chrome clears or corrupts data, this allows for full data restoration. If you’d like help restoring your data or verifying your backups, feel free to reach out to support@sessionbuddy.com. We’re always happy to assist.

We're also working on a cloud storage option that will eliminate this class of issue entirely by keeping your data safely synchronized and recoverable outside the browser.

Please reach out to support@sessionbuddy.com so we can point you in the right direction to get your data back.

UPDATE Nov 17: we recently identified a browser bug that can indeed crash extensions, and it turns out Session Buddy's backup feature is affected by this bug. A workaround will be rolled out soon.

reviews.text: It works for bringing up curated sessions, which I appreciate, but the folder management system is terrible. Every time I want to add a new link to a collection is automatically adds it to a new folder, and then I have to go and "unify folders". Also links cannot be moved between existing folders. It is a terrible design with the limited movement. Either more movement abilities need to be added, or the whole folder structure should be done away with. Not sure what the devs were thinking.
reviews.dev_reply:
UPDATE: in addition to the points made below, the next release will also include the ability to move a selected link up or down within and across folders in a collection by using keyboard shortcuts alt+↑ and alt+↓

That's fair. There's definitely room for improvement here.

Folder management will benefit significantly from the drag/drop feature we're working on. In the meantime, you can copy/paste selected links within or across collections using standard keyboard shortcuts like ctrl+c/ctrl+v or menus. "cut" will be added soon to make moving easier.

Paste preserves folder structure by default, but you can optionally paste copied links into a particular position by right-clicking the folder or link after which you want to insert the links, then clicking Paste.

Lastly, the next release expands the "unify folders" feature such that it considers folder and link selections, allowing you to selectively merge a subset of folders or move a selection of links into a new folder.

reviews.text:
This extension has poor usability and, worse, doesn't work right. 

For usability, it lacks even the most obvious conveniences, like choosing a reasonable default name when saving a session, providing a simple drop down interface, or providing a single keystroke to save the current state or to update the session after changes are made, ... It even warns that it chose an obviously inappropriate keyboard shortcut (cmd-b), but for some reason hasn't fixed this yet.

I have also found this extension to be about as unreliable as any I've ever used. The first time I tried to save sessions, I saved several sessions using variations in what I included, then closed and immediately reopened the extension page, just to make sure it was working. When it reopened, the page was blank, and the sessions never reappeared. On subsequent uses, similar failures are not only not rare, they seem to be the norm. For instance, the last time I attempted to restore as session, of 397 tabs, only 74 were restored.

It would be very unwise for anyone to rely on this extension, or even waste time exploring its use.

I strongly encourage the developer to stop development of this extension and remove it from the extension store, as a service to the community. The last thing we need is more poorly written extensions wasting our time and diluting the extension ecosystem. Please leave the development of extensions to people with the talent and knowledge to do so successfully.

reviews.dev_reply:
Session Buddy lets you choose how to open a collection.

By default it opens a collection as it's organized, creating windows from folders. You can alternatively open all tabs in a single window or the active window as desired. Click the 3-dot menu (upper-right) and select either "Open in one window" or "Open in this window".

There's keyboard shortcuts for this too... you can hold down CTRL (or CMD on Mac) while clicking the "Open" button to open the collection in the active window or SHIFT to open in one window.

And remember, you can always open just a single folder or subset of links by selecting the items you want to open (with Shift or CTRL/CMD key), then clicking "Open selected".

reviews.text: Life saver. Session Buddy is my left-most tab and my command-center. Also, I love that I can save a window and reopen it later to have all the tabs needed for a certain project for as long as I'm working on the project.

Great customer support. And fantastic extension. I would highly recommend this to anyone who frequently opens tabs that they will later on have to re-open. It allows you to label saved sessions as well. I would definitely recommend making a backup quite frequently though as I have personally experienced on a few occasions now, the occurrence of the extension's data being cleared thus causing my entire collections list to be wiped completely. The customer support is amazing though. The issues I have encountered over the years the few times I have had any, the support member helped me via Email very quickly. They made sure to go through my issue thoroughly and guided me through the steps to fix the issue(s) the extension was experiencing. I use the extension using Microsoft Edge. However, I really do wish it was possible to enable the ability for the extension to automatically save current sessions. It can be quite tedious to have to manually run the backup function. Also, if you use the "Restore" function, to import a previous backup file, it can often times say that it has restored collections that it doesn't actually seem to restore for some reason. I assume this will be fixed at some point though.
A useful tool but I really really wish drag and drop was possible! (moving tabs to other windows (or collections) w/o having to copy paste and then go back and delete from the current window)

Agreed! We're looking forward to adding drag and drop. It's on our list of top priorities: https://sessionbuddy.com/roadmap/

In the meantime, the next release (v4.2) will include a Cut action that should make moving tabs and links easier, eliminating the need to go back and delete from the source.

reviews.dev_reply:
To save a tab or any subset of the current session to a new collection, select the desired windows/tabs in "This browser", right-click the selection, and click "Save". Also, if you click the Save button at the top when windows or tabs are selected, the newly-created collection will contain only the selected items.

For links, there is "Copy to new collection" and "Move to new collection".

We have plans to add an "Add to collection" action that presents a list of target collections. In the meantime, there is an easier way to add tabs to collections than "Add from text": simply copy/paste selected tabs from "This browser" directly into any collection. You can use menus or the standard copy/paste keyboard shortcuts. To paste to a specific location, right-click a link and click "Paste".
